newsitem.title: USA: Smart gun to be tested for U.S. police.
newsitem.headline: Smart gun to be tested for U.S. police.

text.p: A "smart" gun that could protect police officers from being shot by their own weapons was demonstrated for members of Congress Wednesday.

The gun was developed by Colt Manufacturing Company, which will test several versions over the next two years. It is unlocked by a radio signal from a receiver worn by the person authorised to use the gun.

"If a criminal steals this gun, it won't work. If a child finds this gun, it won't work. This technology gives me hope that we can figure out a way to prevent gun deaths," said Representative Patricia Schroeder, a Colorado Democrat who attended the demonstration.

Several police officers are killed each year with their own guns during struggles with assailants. In 1993 -- the latest year for which statistics were available -- four police officers were killed with their own guns.
The National Institute of Justice and Sandia National Laboratories are also trying to develop guns that can only be used by their owners.
Other methods being studied include guns that use fingerprint or voice recognition systems to be activated.
Police officers questioned by Sandia said they would like more secure guns if they were reliable and easy to use.
